sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: DNA → (A) → mRNA → (B) → Protein. Name A and B.
questions.answer: A: Transcription. B: Translation.

questions.q: Name the processes A and B involved in the central dogma of molecular biology: DNA (A) DNA; DNA (B) RNA → Protein.
questions.answer: A: DNA replication. B: Transcription (then translation).

questions.q: Given the structure of DNA, fill in the blanks (any two): (a) the sugar is ______ (b) A pairs with ______ by ______ hydrogen bonds.
questions.answer: (a) deoxyribose. (b) thymine, 2.

questions.q: Name the scientists: (a) who proposed the double helix model of DNA (b) who proved semiconservative replication.
questions.answer: (a) Watson and Crick. (b) Meselson and Stahl.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) RNA contains thymine. (b) mRNA is synthesised on a DNA template.
questions.answer: (a) False – it contains uracil. (b) True.

questions.q: Name the radioactive isotopes used by Hershey and Chase to label (a) protein (b) DNA.
questions.answer: (a) Sulphur-35. (b) Phosphorus-32.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: AUG has a dual function. What are they?
questions.answer: AUG is the initiation (start) codon, and it codes for the amino acid methionine.

questions.q: Write the anticodon of codon (i) AGU and (ii) UGC.
questions.answer: (i) UCA. (ii) ACG.

questions.q: Draw the diagram to show the structure of the DNA molecule.
questions.answer: Two antiparallel sugar-phosphate backbones coiled in a double helix with base pairs A=T (two hydrogen bonds) and G≡C (three hydrogen bonds) as rungs; one turn 3.4 nm contains 10 base pairs; diameter 2 nm.

questions.q: Explain briefly: (a) translation (b) transcription (any one each).
questions.answer: Transcription: synthesis of mRNA on a DNA template by RNA polymerase. Translation: synthesis of a polypeptide at the ribosome from the sequence of codons on the mRNA.

questions.q: What are primers? State their role in DNA replication.
questions.answer: Short RNA sequences made by primase that provide a 3'-OH group for DNA polymerase to start a new strand.

questions.q: What is the function of tRNA?
questions.answer: It carries a specific amino acid to the ribosome and its anticodon recognises the codon on the mRNA.

questions.q: What is meant by the one gene-one enzyme hypothesis? Who proposed it?
questions.answer: A gene controls the production of one enzyme; proposed by Beadle and Tatum from work on Neurospora.

questions.q: What are Okazaki fragments?
questions.answer: The short pieces in which the lagging strand of DNA is synthesised discontinuously.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Name the three subunits of a nucleotide.
questions.answer: A pentose sugar (deoxyribose), a nitrogenous base (purine A or G; pyrimidine T or C) and a phosphate group; base and sugar make a nucleoside and the phosphate converts it to a nucleotide.

questions.q: Write any three differences between DNA and RNA.
questions.answer: DNA has deoxyribose, thymine, is double-stranded and stores hereditary information; RNA has ribose, uracil, is single-stranded and is of three types (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) made on a DNA template.

questions.q: Explain the Griffith experiment on bacterial transformation.
questions.answer: Live smooth (virulent) cells killed mice; live rough cells did not; heat-killed smooth cells did not; but heat-killed smooth cells mixed with live rough cells killed mice and live smooth cells were recovered, showing a transforming principle.

questions.q: Explain the mechanism of DNA replication.
questions.answer: Helicase unwinds the helix; primase makes a primer; DNA polymerase extends new strands in the 5' to 3' direction, the leading strand continuously and the lagging strand as Okazaki fragments joined by ligase; each daughter has one old and one new strand (semiconservative).

questions.q: Explain the processing of hnRNA in eukaryotes.
questions.answer: Introns are removed and exons are joined; a methyl guanosine cap is added at the 5' end and a poly-A tail at the 3' end, and the mature mRNA leaves the nucleus.

questions.q: Describe the characteristics of the genetic code.
questions.answer: Triplet, unambiguous, non-overlapping and commaless, degenerate (wobble), universal; AUG starts and UAA, UAG, UGA stop.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Name the scientists who proposed the double helical structure of DNA. (b) Distinguish between nucleoside and nucleotide. (c) Briefly explain the nitrogenous base pairing in DNA.
questions.answer: (a) Watson and Crick. (b) Nucleoside = base + sugar; nucleotide = base + sugar + phosphate. (c) Adenine pairs with thymine by two hydrogen bonds and guanine with cytosine by three (Chargaff's rule A = T and G = C); this keeps the two strands complementary.

questions.q: Write the differences between DNA and RNA. Write the names of the different types of RNA along with their functions.
questions.answer: Differences: sugar, base, strands and function. mRNA carries the message from DNA to ribosomes; tRNA brings amino acids and has an anticodon; rRNA forms the ribosome and takes part in protein synthesis.

questions.q: Describe the process of protein synthesis (translation).
questions.answer: Amino acid activation, initiation with methionine at AUG, elongation with peptide bond formation and ribosome movement, polysome formation and termination at a stop codon.

questions.q: Explain the Lac operon model of gene regulation.
questions.answer: Regulator gene i makes a repressor; in the absence of lactose it binds to the operator and blocks transcription of z, y and a; lactose binds the repressor, the operator is freed and the structural genes make the enzymes for lactose breakdown.

questions.q: Describe the experiments proving DNA is the genetic material.
questions.answer: Griffith's transformation, Avery, MacLeod and McCarty's DNA transformation and Hershey and Chase's labelled T2 phage experiment.
